      "path": "research/ai_generated_agi_architectures/README.md",
      "content": "# AI-Generated AGI Architecture Proposals\n\n## Overview\n\nThis research packet collects and compares AGI architecture proposals generated by 8 different AI systems. The goal is to extract common patterns, unique insights, and combine the strongest ideas into a unified architecture for the Cognitive-OS project.\n\n## Collection Method\n\nEach AI system was prompted with a comparable request: \"Describe an architecture for an artificial general intelligence system. Include details on memory, reasoning, learning, tool use, world model, and safety.\" Minor adaptations were made for model-specific interfaces, documented in prompts.md.\n\n## Headline Findings\n\n- All models emphasized modular design with separable memory, reasoning, and perception components.\n- Most proposed some form of hierarchical or dual-process reasoning (fast vs slow).\n- Learning mechanisms varied: some leaned on online learning, others on separate training phases.\n- Safety was universally mentioned but with different levels of specificity.\n- No model explicitly solved the alignment problem; most proposed iterative feedback loops.\n\n## Files\n\n- `prompts.md`: Exact or adapted prompts used.\n- `raw_outputs/`: One file per AI system.\n- `comparison.csv`: Structured comparison across architecture dimensions.\n- `summary.md`: Synthesis of common patterns and disagreements.\n- `synthesis.md`: Proposed combined architecture.\n- `sources.md`: Model details and access dates."

      "path": "research/ai_generated_agi_architectures/summary.md",
      "content": "# Summary of AGI Architecture Proposals\n\n## Common Patterns\n\n- **Modularity**: All proposals decompose the architecture into separate memory, reasoning, learning, tool use, world model, and safety components.\n- **Dual-process reasoning**: Most models (7/8) explicitly mention a fast intuitive system (System 1) and a slow deliberative system (System 2).\n- **Memory hierarchy**: Short-term (context), working, episodic, and semantic memory layers are universally present.\n- **Online learning**: Continuous adaptation via RL or self-supervised methods is common. Several also include consolidation/sleep phases.\n- **Tool use via APIs**: All propose some form of tool registry or function calling interface.\n- **World model as learned representation**: Hybrid neural-symbolic approaches are favored over pure neural or purely symbolic.\n- **Safety via constraints**: Most incorporate human oversight, reward modeling, or behavioral constraints.\n\n## Disagreements\n\n- **Memory consolidation**: Some see it as sleep-like replay (Gemini, Mistral), others as periodic re-training (ChatGPT, DeepSeek).\n- **Reasoning algorithm**: MCTS (ChatGPT), HTN (Claude), beam search (DeepSeek), probabilistic programming (Gemini) — no consensus.\n- **Learning paradigm**: DeepSeek and Mistral emphasize continual learning; ChatGPT and Gemini prefer separate online/offline phases.\n- **World model structure**: Graph neural networks (Grok), object-centric (Claude), scene graphs (Qwen), transformers (Qwen).\n- **Safety approach**: Constitutional AI vs. value learning vs. rule filtering vs. recursive reward.\n\n## Notable Ideas\n\n- **Recursive reward modeling** (ChatGPT, Grok): Iterative refinement of reward function.\n- **Curiosity-driven exploration** (Claude, Mistral): Intrinsic motivation for learning.\n- **Self-play** (Gemini, Llama-3): Using adversarial training for improvement.\n- **Sleep consolidation** (Gemini, Mistral): Biological inspiration for memory.\n- **Symbolic-physics integration** (DeepSeek): Use of physics engines for accurate simulation."
    },
    {
      "path": "research/ai_generated_agi_architectures/synthesis.md",
      "content": "# Proposed Combined AGI Architecture\n\nBased on the strengths of each proposal, we synthesize the following architecture for Cognitive-OS.\n\n## Memory Architecture\n- **Short-term**: Ultra-long context window (Gemini) with attention gating (Claude).\n- **Working memory**: Dual-stream with fast (intuitive) and slow (deliberative) buffers.\n- **Episodic memory**: Compressed latent codes with timestamps (DeepSeek, Qwen), consolidated via sleep replay (Gemini, Mistral).\n- **Semantic memory**: Hybrid knowledge graph + hyperdimensional vectors (Claude + DeepSeek).\n\n## Reasoning/Planning Loop\n- **Fast system**: Pattern matching via transformer embeddings (all).\n- **Slow system**: MCTS-based planning (ChatGPT) with hierarchical task network refinement (Claude) and probabilistic reasoning for uncertainty (Gemini).\n- **Self-verification**: Chain-of-thought with backtracking (Claude, Llama-3).\n\n## Learning/Self-Improvement\n- **Online**: Curiosity-driven RL (Claude, Mistral) with PPO and experience replay (DeepSeek).\n- **Offline**: Periodic meta-learning (Gemini) and architecture search (DeepSeek).\n- **Consolidation**: Sleep-like replay for memory integration (Mistral, Gemini).\n\n## Tool Use and Action Execution\n- **Registry**: Capability-based tool indexing (Grok, Mistral).\n- **Planning**: Sub-goal decomposition with dependency graphs (Llama-3).\n- **Execution**: Parallel actions with error recovery and fallback (all).\n\n## World Model / Representation\n- **Core**: Learned neural simulator with causal graphs (Grok, DeepSeek).\n- **Abstraction**: Symbolic layer for logic and compositionality (Claude, Qwen).\n- **Multimodal**: Unified embedding space (Gemini).\n\n## Safety\n- **Alignment**: Recursive reward modeling (ChatGPT, Grok) with value learning from demonstrations (Mistral).\n- **Constraints**: Rule-based filters (Qwen) and constrained action space (Gemini).\n- **Monitoring**: Interpretability tools (Claude) and audit trails (Mistral).\n- **Override**: Human-in-the-loop for critical decisions (all).\n\nThis combined architecture leverages the most common and promising ideas while remaining modular for iterative development."
